depicts: Colour-washed Sanborn fire-insurance plan of the Union Depot and Ferry House at the foot of Market Street, drawn looking down on the building and the water. The long shed runs across the top of the sheet between East St. S. and East St. N.; below it, six wedge-shaped ferry slips project into open water labelled 'Bay of San Francisco'.
details: Each slip carries the name of the line that used it: Ferry Slip No.2 NORTH PAC. COAST R.R. SAUSALITO; No.3 S.F. & N. PAC. R.R. TIBURON; No.4 SOUTH PAC. CO. OAKLAND ETC.; No.5 S. PAC. COAST S.P.CO. ALAMEDA ETC.; No.6 SOUTH PAC. CO. EXTRA SLIP. Between the slips sit Freight Sheds 'M', 'N' and 'O'. Inside the building the plan names two long WAITING ROOMs, a MAIN PASSAGE, ticket offices, a newspaper depot, a P.O. station, and on the upper floor the STATE BOARD OF TRADE EXHIBIT HALL and the STATE MINING BUREAU EXHIBIT HALL. A band across the front reads 'PASSAGE TO UPPER DECK OF FERRIES'. Compass rose bottom right.
visible_text: UNION DEPOT AND FERRY HOUSE / EAST ST. S. / EAST ST. N. / Seawall Section 8B / Seawall Section 8A / FERRY SLIP No.2 NORTH PAC. COAST R.R. SAUSALITO / FERRY SLIP No.3 S.F.& N.PAC. R.R. TIBURON / FERRY SLIP No.4 SOUTH PAC. CO. OAKLAND ETC. / FERRY SLIP No.5 S. PAC. COAST S.P.CO. ALAMEDA ETC. / FERRY SLIP No.6 SOUTH PAC. CO. EXTRA SLIP / Bay of San Francisco
notes: The single most literal illustration of the pre-bridge system: the Sausalito and Tiburon slips are named on the drawing, alongside the Oakland and Alameda ones.

attribution: Miscellaneous Items in High Demand, PPOC, Library of Congress
depicts: Elevated view north-east over downtown San Francisco with a Antoinette-type monoplane banking in the upper left of the frame. The Ferry Building clock tower stands at the centre of the waterfront; behind it the open bay, Yerba Buena Island and the East Bay hills.
details: A steam ferry is berthed at the left edge of the waterfront and a freighter lies off the piers at right; masts of sailing ships crowd the northern wharves. Painted roof signs on the low blocks below read OWL and GILT EDGE WHISKIES. The city is still low-rise: only a handful of ten-storey blocks stand between the camera and the water.
visible_text: Roof signs: OWL; GILT EDGE WHISKIES; THE A. LIETZ CO.; ONY LUNG & CO.
notes: Hubert Latham's 1911 flight over San Francisco. Useful for a 1910s establishing shot of the city and its ferry waterfront.

attribution: California. Board of State Harbor Commissioners for San Francisco Harbor
depicts: Halftone plate from the Board of State Harbor Commissioners' 1916 biennial report: the Ferry Building seen from up Market Street, three-quarters on, with its long arcaded front running away to the right and the clock tower at centre.
details: The forecourt is full of period traffic — open touring cars parked nose-in along the arcade, motor trucks, a horse team, and knots of pedestrians crossing the streetcar tracks. Smoke rises from a stack on the shed roof at the right. A billboard on the left reads RAINIER THE HOME BEER. Bare hills rise behind the Embarcadero.
visible_text: Billboard: RAINIER / THE HOME BEER
notes: An official-report image of the terminal at the moment the bridge idea was first being floated (1916-18).

depicts: A US Signal Corps photograph on its original archival mount: the 67th Coast Artillery Regiment marching in column of fours along the Embarcadero past a dense civilian crowd, with the Ferry Building clock tower and its arcaded sheds filling the right-hand background.
details: A cloth banner strung across the street reads 'The PEOPLE of San Francisco WELCOME YOU HOME'. The soldiers carry rifles at the slope; women in long coats and hats press in from the right where the police line has clearly given way. An ornate multi-globe streetlamp stands in the right foreground. The mount carries the caption typed at left.
visible_text: Banner: The PEOPLE of San Francisco WELCOME YOU HOME. Mount: UNDERWOOD & UNDERWOOD / 165-WW / 67TH REGIMENT GREETED IN SAN FRANCISCO. Police lines formed little resistance to joyous and boistrous San Francisco crowds when gallant 67th regiment, Coast Artillery, arrived home.
notes: Shows the Ferry Building as the city's civic front door — the place where arrivals and departures were staged.

depicts: Photochrom postcard, portrait format, of the Union Ferry Depot from the Embarcadero: the clock tower rises almost the full height of the card above the arcaded stone front of the terminal.
details: Both clock faces are picked out with gold hands. At street level a covered horse-drawn wagon stands in front of the arches and a second wagon blurs past on the left; a few pedestrians and a line of low bollards separate the paving from the cobbled roadway. The foreground is unpaved and rutted. A caption is printed faintly along the bottom edge.
visible_text: Faint caption along lower edge: 'Union Ferry Depot, San Francisco.'
notes: Portrait orientation — a constraint for a 16:9 deck, but the tower fills the frame.

attribution: Miscellaneous Items in High Demand, PPOC, Library of Congress
depicts: Wide panoramic photograph, reproduced with its full negative border and grey mount, of the Ferry Building at the evening rush. The building runs the whole width of the frame; the plaza in front is thick with people.
details: Hundreds of commuters stream diagonally across the open plaza toward the terminal. Two open streetcars stand at the loading platform in front of the arcade; a line of early motor cars is parked nose-in beside them, mixed with horse-drawn buggies and a horse cart at the right. A banner reading 1915 hangs on the clock tower, advertising the coming Panama-Pacific Exposition. Ships' masts crowd the wharves at the far left.
visible_text: Caption in the negative, lower left: NO. 618 EVENING HOUR, FERRY BLDG. Lower right: COPYRIGHTED 1912. R.J. WATERS & CO. Banner on tower: 1915
notes: The definitive image of the ferry-era commute — the crowd is the subject. R.J. Waters panoramic negative.

depicts: An undivided-back Detroit Photographic Co. postcard, printed with wide cream margins: a three-quarter view of the Ferry Building from the Embarcadero, tower left of centre, the arcade receding to the right.
details: Horse-drawn traffic only — a pair of white horses pulling a wagon at the left, a covered buggy in the middle distance, and at the right what appears to be a steam traction engine or road roller. A lone man in a dark suit walks across the muddy, puddled foreground. Ships' masts show over the sheds at far right.
visible_text: FERRY BUILDING, SAN FRANCISCO. / 5654 COPYRIGHT, 1901, BY DETROIT PHOTOGRAPHIC CO.
notes: Dates the terminal at the turn of the century, before the 1906 earthquake.

depicts: A linen-finish colour postcard looking down on the Ferry Building from the north-west, with the newly completed San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge sweeping across the whole background.
details: The bridge's twin suspension spans and Yerba Buena anchorage dominate the sky behind the clock tower. In the foreground the Embarcadero is jammed with green and cream streetcars on the loop, buses and cars; the elevated ferry loop ramp curves across the bottom of the frame. The finger piers north of the building are drawn in red and green. Colours are the exaggerated pastels of a 1930s linen card.
visible_text: '87:—FERRY BUILDING, SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA
notes: Post-bridge, and useful for the 'after' beat: the fixed link is now the backdrop and the ferry terminal has become a streetcar interchange.

depicts: Halftone plate captioned 'FERRY BUILDING, SAN FRANCISCO', an elevated three-quarter view from the south with the tower at right and the arcade running back to the left.
details: A paddle ferry lies in the slip on the far left of the frame with steam up, its stack smoking. In front of the building horse-drawn wagons and several open-platform streetcars stand on the plaza; telegraph poles and a mass of ship masts fill the right background. The plaza surface is unpaved.
visible_text: Caption below the plate: FERRY BUILDING, SAN FRANCISCO.
notes: From the 1907 California Blue Book. One of the few frames in the pool that shows a ferry actually berthed in a slip.

attribution: Related names: Brown, A Page Swain, Edward Holmes, Howard C Polk, Willis
depicts: Interior of the Ferry Building's second-floor nave, looking the length of the hall. A double row of arched windows runs down both sides under an exposed steel truss roof with a continuous glazed ridge skylight.
details: The hall is completely empty of people — a corridor of bare terrazzo floor with a line of potted palms in square tubs down the centre, receding to a lit arch at the far end. A small sign on the left wall reads 'HARBOR COMMISSION ENGINEERS OFFICE'. The image is a copy negative and is laterally reversed; the HABS number is written along the bottom edge, mirrored.
visible_text: HABS No. CAL-1910 (written on the negative, reversed)
notes: The grand nave without its crowd — the same space that 50,000 commuters a week passed through. Reversed negative.

depicts: Interior of the State Mining Bureau museum on an upper floor of the Ferry Building, looking down a long central aisle flanked on both sides by glazed display cases of ore and mineral specimens.
details: Framed pictures and upright cabinets stand between the cases; the great arched terminal windows are visible top left and top right with their diagonal glazing bars, which is what identifies the room as being inside the Ferry Building. A dozen or so visitors in period dress — men in bowlers, women in wide hats — lean over the cases in the middle distance.
notes: Reproduced in 'Looters of the Public Domain' (1907). The Ferry Building did double duty as a public exhibition hall.

depicts: Large-format HABS architectural record photograph, portrait format: a straight-on elevation of the Ferry Building's Embarcadero (west) front, with the clock tower centred and the arcade running symmetrically to both edges.
details: Clean, deliberately undramatic documentation lighting. Cars of the late 1950s are parked along the kerb; the arcade arches are shaded and empty. The tower's clock faces read a little after ten.
notes: Jack Boucher for HABS. A neutral, high-resolution reference elevation of the building; post-bridge, when the terminal had lost its traffic.

depicts: The Southern Pacific ferry SAN MATEO under way just off the Ferry Building, seen broadside from the water. Her name is painted along the white hull below the passenger deck; the Ferry Building clock tower rises directly behind her.
details: Black smoke streams aft from the single funnel, which carries the Southern Pacific herald. The long line of pilings and the ferry slip fencing runs across the left of the frame; a low warehouse block stands at far left. Two painted roof signs are legible on the shoreline behind — a large '57' (Heinz) at the left and WELLMAN COFFEE at the right. Telegraph Hill rises in the haze on the right.
visible_text: On the hull: SOUTHERN PACIFIC / SAN MATEO. On the negative, top: HAER No. WA-17-35. Roof signs: 57; WELLMAN COFFEE
notes: Southern Pacific ferry operating out of the Ferry Building in the exact period the essay covers.

attribution: Mark Hogan from San Francisco, USA
depicts: Colour 35 mm slide taken from the top of the Mark Hopkins Hotel looking north-east over downtown San Francisco to the bay. The Bay Bridge crosses the whole width of the upper frame; Yerba Buena and Alcatraz sit in the water beyond.
details: The Ferry Building tower is now a small white spike at the centre of the frame, dwarfed by the office blocks around it — a striking measure of how far the terminal had receded by the late 1950s. A large SP roof sign (Southern Pacific) stands on a building at right of centre. The slide shows dust specks and emulsion scratches across the sky.
visible_text: Roof sign: SP
notes: Post-bridge. Good for the closing beat: the fixed links won and the ferry terminal became scenery.

depicts: Photograph looking toward the Ferry Building shortly after the April 1906 earthquake. The clock tower is wrapped in a full timber scaffold from about half its height to the top; the arcaded front stretches across the frame behind.
details: The foreground is a rubble field: heaps of broken brick and masonry, loose timbers laid across the mud, and two large white relief tents pitched at the left with people trading in front of them. A sign on the tent reads PACIFIC COAST ... A single-truck streetcar numbered 1391, destination sign '19th AVE', stands at the right; a second car is behind it. Men in bowler hats, women in long skirts and a boy walk toward the terminal along the churned dirt roadway.
visible_text: Streetcar: 19TH AVE / 1391. Tent sign (partly legible): PACIFIC COAST... Negative number lower left: 95106
notes: H.D. Chadwick, NARA. The terminal survived 1906 and was the city's lifeline while the streets were still rubble.

depicts: Hand-coloured divided-back postcard of the Southern Pacific ferry OAKLAND under way on the bay, seen broadside from the port side, with the SP wharf sheds and other shipping behind her.
details: Two funnels, a tall walking-beam gallows amidships, and two full passenger decks with a continuous run of windows. OAKLAND is painted large on the white hull side and SOUTHERN PACIFIC in small letters above it. The sea is rendered in flat green, the sky in printed cloud.
visible_text: Card title, red script upper left: Southern Pacific Ferry Boat 'Oakland.' San Francisco, Cal. On the hull: SOUTHERN PACIFIC / OAKLAND
notes: A named Southern Pacific bay ferry as the travelling public knew her, on a souvenir card.

depicts: A worn, torn sepia photograph taken from the deck of a boat inside a ferry slip, looking in toward the shore. The Ferry Building's clock tower stands in the middle distance completely encased in scaffolding — the building is still under construction.
details: The slip's timber fenders and pile walls run away on both sides toward the terminal shed. A large board fixed to the wall at left reads TELEGRAPH CABLE CROSSING. A small cupola stands on the corner of the shed. A boat's bow with rigging and a bollard occupies the left foreground; capstan gear the right. The print is creased, torn along the top edge and has a piece missing from the lower right corner.
visible_text: Sign on wall: TELEGRAPH CABLE CROSSING
notes: The Ferry Building going up in 1898 — the terminal that would define the next forty years of bay travel, photographed from a slip.

attribution: Photographer unknown, Wells Fargo Bank Historical Museum
depicts: The Union Depot and Ferry House of 1875 — the wooden predecessor of the Ferry Building — seen from up Market Street: a long open-arched shed with a small square clock cupola on the ridge.
details: Painted along the fascia above the arches is a list of destinations reached from the depot: SAN JOSE, SACRAMENTO, LOS ANGELES, CHICAGO, NEW YORK, with a STATION POST OFFICE sign at the right end. Three or four horse-drawn streetcars stand on the turntable apron in front, one lettered for a Market Street line; the rest of the forecourt is crowded with wagons, hansom cabs and hay carts with their horses in the shafts. Men stand in groups on the loading apron.
visible_text: On the fascia: ...SAN JOSE / SACRAMENTO / LOS ANGELES / CHICAGO / NEW YORK; STATION AND POST OFFICE
notes: The old wooden ferry house, replaced by the 1898 Ferry Building. Wells Fargo Bank Historical Museum copy.

depicts: Colour postcard of the Southern Pacific train ferry SOLANO crossing the Carquinez Strait, photographed from a hillside above the water. The town of Benicia and its long wharves fill the far shore.
details: The vessel is enormous and low in the water, with four tall black funnels in two pairs and a row of freight cars visible on her deck; she is throwing a broad white wake. Foliage frames the lower left corner. Printed caption in orange type across the bottom margin.
visible_text: The Solano, largest ferryboat in the world, crossing the Straits of Carquinez from Benicia to Port Costa.
notes: Publisher's claim 'largest ferryboat in the world' — useful shorthand for the scale of the pre-bridge ferry system, though this is the Carquinez train ferry, not a bay commuter boat.

depicts: Colour postcard of the Key Route ferry terminal (the Key System Mole) photographed from a departing boat: the yellow and red terminal building sits at the end of a long trestle pier out in open water.
details: A great dark arched slip mouth opens in the centre of the terminal front. Two ferries lie alongside at the right. Two small sailing dinghies cross the choppy foreground water, one dark-hulled and one white. The bay is rendered in vivid turquoise with a heavy printed wave texture. Hills of the far shore on the horizon.
visible_text: 1696 — KEY ROUTE TERMINAL FROM THE BAY, BERKELEY, CALIFORNIA.
notes: Edward H. Mitchell card. The trans-bay competitor system: everything on the water before either bridge.

depicts: Albumen cabinet photograph looking straight down the deck of the Central Pacific train ferry SOLANO from inside the slip. Two railway tracks run from the camera up the deck; a locomotive and cars stand under the centre gantry.
details: Roughly twenty men — crew and yard workers in waistcoats, work shirts and hats — are posed standing along and between the tracks, most looking at the camera. The pilot house high on the superstructure carries the name SOLANO in large letters. Two tall funnels flank it and curved lattice gangways arch over the deck. Timber pile walls of the slip rise on both sides; a bare hillside shows over the right-hand wall. Lifeboats hang in davits either side.
visible_text: On the pilot house: SOLANO. Handwritten in the negative, lower right: C.P. TRANSFER STEAMER, PORT COSTA, CAL. C.R. SAVAGE PHOTO. Below the mount: Brigham Young University Lee Library L. Tom Perry Special Collections; MSS P 24
notes: Charles Roscoe Savage. The men on the deck give the vessel its scale.

depicts: A stereo card — the same view printed twice side by side — of the Central Pacific ferry EL CAPITAN lying at her slip at the Oakland terminus, seen from the shore looking down the length of the wooden pier.
details: A plank walkway with a line of piling stumps runs diagonally away from the camera into the middle distance where the ferry lies bow-on to the right. Wooden freight sheds with plank siding and small-paned windows fill the left half of the frame; a barrel and a hand truck sit on the boards. The ferry has a tall single funnel, an open promenade deck and a pilot house forward; a solitary figure stands on her guard rail.
visible_text: Name faintly on the hull: EL CAPITAN
notes: Thomas Houseworth & Co. The oldest ferry photograph in the pool. As a stereo card it is naturally split down the middle; a single half would need cropping.

depicts: High oblique aerial looking west-north-west across the East Bay flats toward San Francisco. The half-built Bay Bridge causeway drives out from Oakland across the tideland in the centre of the frame; the city, the bay and the Marin hills fill the top third.
details: Two slender Bay Bridge tower legs stand alone out in the water left of Yerba Buena Island, with no cable or deck between them yet. Far away on the right horizon, two more thin verticals mark the Golden Gate Bridge towers, also still cableless. Alcatraz sits at the right. A ferry trails a white wake near the Key System mole at left of centre; the mole's ferry slips and a working dredge are visible. Below, the grid streets, rail yards and factories of West Oakland run to the bottom edge.
visible_text: Caption in the negative, bottom: (03-321-15)(4-8-35-10:30A.)(12-5500) EAST APPROACH OAKLAND BAY BRIDGE.
notes: Both bridges under construction at once, with ferries still running underneath — the exact moment the ferry era ends. Dated 8 April 1935.

depicts: High oblique aerial over the Oakland estuary and the East Bay shoreline, looking east toward the hills with Mount Diablo on the skyline. Long timber moles and rail piers project out into the shallow bay across the middle of the frame.
details: Two ferries are under way in the open water of the foreground, each drawing a long white wake behind it; a third small boat sits further out. Strings of freight cars stand on the piers. Behind the waterfront, the low residential grid of Oakland spreads back to Lake Merritt and the small downtown cluster of towers.
visible_text: Caption in the negative, bottom: (O-791-32M-23)(1-27-32-10:35A.M.)(12-2000) [S]E OAKLAND CALIF.
notes: Dated 27 January 1932 — the ferry system at its peak, three years before either bridge opened.

depicts: Near-vertical aerial photograph of the Key System Mole: the terminal building and its slips sit at the tip of a long causeway that curves in from the top right corner across otherwise empty water.
details: Six ferries are berthed in a row along the north side of the pier, moored side by side like cards in a hand, with a seventh alongside the terminal front at the bottom. A train sits on the causeway approach. A white blur near the top of the frame is a moving vessel. The composition is almost abstract — most of the frame is flat grey water. A circular rubber stamp is printed in the lower left corner.
visible_text: Stamp: 15TH PHOTO SECTION / OFFICIAL PHOTOGRAPH / AIR SERVICE
notes: US Army Air Service photograph. Six ferries tied up in one frame — the clearest single image of the sheer fleet size.

depicts: Portrait-format shipyard photograph: the ferry EUREKA in dry dock at the Moore Dry Dock Company, Oakland, receiving a newly built walking beam. The great cast beam hangs on slings above the open engine casing.
details: Riggers stand on staging around the beam; the ferry's superstructure and stack rise behind. Heavy timber shoring and dockside cranes frame the shot.
notes: Dated 24 July 1926. The maintenance side of the ferry fleet — the machinery that had to be kept running.

depicts: Modern colour photograph looking through the entrance gantry of Hyde Street Pier, San Francisco, straight at the bow of the preserved ferry EUREKA framed in the opening.
details: A large black-on-white sign across the gantry reads HYDE ST PIER. The ferry's white pilot house carries a gold-lettered EUREKA nameboard, with a US flag on a staff in front of it. Two conical white bow bollards flank the gangway; green mesh safety fencing runs along both sides. A metal shield sign at the right reads REDWOOD HIGHWAY U.S. [101]. Deep blue cloudless sky; bleached timber decking in the foreground.
visible_text: HYDE ST PIER / EUREKA / REDWOOD HIGHWAY U.S. 101 / 'THE NUMBER OF VISITORS ON THIS VESSEL NOT TO EXCEED 487 PERSONS.'
notes: A surviving bay ferry, and the Redwood Highway shield is the direct visual link: US 101 north out of San Francisco ran onto a boat before it ran onto the bridge.

depicts: Photograph of a printed ferry restaurant menu displayed aboard the EUREKA, shot straight on. Tall, narrow portrait format.
details: A period menu card listing dishes and prices for a single day's service afloat, printed in plain type with a dated heading.
visible_text: Menu heading dated August 14, 1940
notes: Ephemera: what it was like to eat on the boat during the crossing. Strongly portrait — full-frame use would need a treatment.

depicts: Hand-coloured divided-back postcard: a Key Route ferry, broadside on, sliding into the slip at the Oakland mole, photographed from the pier railing in the foreground.
details: The ferry is painted the same ochre yellow as the terminal, with two full decks of windows and a tall centre stack topped with a lattice gallows frame. Heavy yellow timber fender clusters stand in the water between the camera and the boat. On the right, the overhead trolley wire, catenary poles and train shed of the Key Route pier run away into the distance, with electric interurban cars visible inside. A pale civic-looking building stands behind the boat.
visible_text: O. 46 / Ferry Boat entering the Key Route Slip, Oakland, Cal.
notes: Shows the ferry-to-electric-train transfer that made the trans-bay commute work.

attribution: Arkiv i Nordland from Bodø, Norway
depicts: Colour postcard of the train ferry SOLANO seen head-on inside her slip, bow toward the camera, with a steam locomotive and two passenger cars standing on her deck.
details: Four tall funnels rise in pairs either side of the pilot house, which carries the name SOLANO on a board. Curved lattice gangways arch over the tracks. Around forty men, boys and one woman in a white dress are grouped on the open bow deck around the locomotive's pilot. Timber pile walls of the slip rise steeply on both sides of the frame. Bold gold lettering runs across the hull below the deck.
visible_text: 1548 — Southern Pacific Co's Ferryboat 'Solano' Port Costa-Benicia, California. LARGEST FERRYBOAT IN THE WORLD. On the hull: SOLANO OF SAN FRANCISCO
notes: A whole train riding a boat — the most vivid image of what a fixed link would eventually replace. Card is creased through the lower left.

depicts: A James Bard ship portrait in oils: the sidewheel steamer SAN RAFAEL under way in profile, facing left, on a green-blue sea under a warm hazy sky. Low hills close both sides of the background and small sailing craft dot the middle distance.
details: Bard's characteristic flat, precise draughtsmanship — every window, stanchion and rail picked out. The paddlebox is painted with a radiating sunburst and the name SAN RAFAEL in dark letters along the white deckhouse below. Two long swallow-tail flags fly from the masts: one at the bow lettered S.R., one at the stern lettered SAN RAFAEL. A gilded eagle finial tops the foremast. Whitewater churns at the paddle wheel.
visible_text: On the hull: SAN RAFAEL. Bow flag: S.R. Stern flag: SAN RAFAEL. Signed lower right: J. BARD, N.Y. 1877
notes: The San Rafael ran the Marin ferry service; she was sunk in a collision off Alcatraz in 1901.

depicts: A cropped horizontal strip from an aerial photograph of the Key System Mole and the West Oakland waterfront, looking north-west. The mole runs out from the shore across the right of the frame into open water.
details: At the top right corner the trestle of the Bay Bridge approach is visible under construction, marching out across the water. Vast fans of rail yard track spread across the left half of the frame behind the shoreline; the dense street grid of West Oakland fills the bottom. Ferry slips and pier structures line the tip of the mole. Low contrast, hazy.
notes: Dated c.1934 — the bridge trestle arriving alongside the ferry mole it would kill.

depicts: Wide letterbox halftone from Electric Railway Journal: the interior train shed at the end of the Key Route pier, looking along the platforms. A steel truss roof with glazed panels spans the full width.
details: Two four-car trains of wooden electric interurban cars stand at the platforms, one with car 502 leading and another car numbered 504 at the right edge; both carry roof trolley poles under the overhead wire. White-painted picket fencing and ticket gates line the left-hand platform, with lettered signboards over each gate. The concrete platforms are empty of passengers.
visible_text: Car numbers 502 and 504 on the dashes
notes: From the 1909 Electric Railway Journal. The shed where trains and boats met.

depicts: White-border colour postcard looking down the length of the Key Route Pier from a high vantage at the terminal end. The trestle and its multiple tracks curve away to the left into the distance; ferries are berthed along the right.
details: A rake of maroon interurban cars stands on the left-hand track; overhead catenary poles march down the pier. Two large ferries lie in the slips on the right, one with SAN FRANCISCO lettered on her deckhouse in the near foreground and a carved eagle on her pilot house. Small red-roofed pier shacks and stacked lumber occupy the middle foreground. Far shore hills across the top.
visible_text: The Key Route Pier, San Francisco-Oakland-Berkeley, Cal. On a ferry's deckhouse: SAN FRANCISCO
notes: Shows train and ferry in the same frame at the point of transfer.

depicts: Colour postcard of the Key Route ferry waiting room at the end of the pier: a large open timber hall with a heavy exposed truss roof and painted post-and-beam structure.
details: Rows of dark wooden benches with high backs fill the floor, all empty. Potted banana plants and small palms in tubs stand between the white picket screens. Through the screens on the left the slip and daylight are visible; on the right, glazed windows look out over the water. A signboard on the far wall reads ...OAKLAND & SAN... The printed caption runs in red across the bottom left corner.
visible_text: 4491 Oakland, Cal. 'Key Route' Ferry waiting room, end of Pier
notes: Postmarked 1909. The waiting room is the thing a bridge abolishes — you sat and waited for a boat.

depicts: Colour postcard of a Key Route ferry lying alongside the Oakland mole terminal at dusk, seen broadside from the water with the terminal building at the right of the frame.
details: A long plume of black smoke drifts back from the single tall stack across a green-grey sky. The vessel is printed in dark brown-black with two full rows of lit windows. The cream and yellow terminal building with its arched slip mouth stands at the right end of the pier. The bay in the foreground is rendered in fine printed ripples. A copyright line runs vertically up the left margin.
visible_text: Key Route Ferry Boat, Oakland, Cal. Left margin, vertical: Copyright, 1907, by Pillsbury Picture Co.
notes: Postmarked 1911. Pillsbury Picture Company.

depicts: Colour postcard of the Southern Pacific train ferry SOLANO under way on San Francisco Bay, seen broadside from the port quarter, throwing white water from her paddle.
details: Four black funnels smoke heavily against a pale sky. The lower hull is painted deep red-brown, the deckhouse white with SOLANO lettered on it beside a decorated paddlebox. Freight cars are just visible on the deck aft. Low tan hills run along the horizon behind. The card is a Norwegian-archive scan, sent from the USA to Træna, Norway.
visible_text: 261 — S.P.R.R. CO.'S FERRYBOAT 'SOLANO', SAN FRANCISCO BAY, CALIFORNIA. (LARGEST IN THE WORLD.) On the hull: SOLANO
notes: Arkiv i Nordland copy of a card mailed from the USA to Norway — the ferries were what visitors sent home.

depicts: A Richmond-San Rafael Ferry Company advertising postcard: three inset colour photographs of the company's ferries arranged on a cream ground, with advertising copy set in the spaces between them.
details: The top centre inset, captioned CITY OF SAN RAFAEL, shows a ferry bow-on with her open decks packed shoulder-to-shoulder with passengers. Lower left, CITY OF RICHMOND under way past a headland; lower right, CHARLES VAN DAMME. A small circular company logo sits between the lower two. All three boats are painted the same red-brown. Copy blocks left and right list the destinations served.
visible_text: TRAVEL BY THE SHORTEST ROUTE. / To points in East Bay Territory, Santa Clara and San Joaquin Valleys and So. California. / To Resorts of Russian River, Marin, Sonoma, Mendocino and Lake Counties and Northern California. / CITY OF SAN RAFAEL / CITY OF RICHMOND / CHARLES VAN DAMME / RICHMOND SAN RAFAEL FERRY CO. / 103505
notes: Marin-bound ferry advertising from the mid-1920s, selling exactly the northern-California access the bridge campaign promised to improve. 'Travel by the shortest route' is the ferry companies' own pitch.

depicts: A second, tighter reproduction of James Bard's 1877 oil portrait of the Marin sidewheel ferry SAN RAFAEL, profile facing left, sunlit against a pale sky with hills either side.
details: Same composition as the other Bard in the pool but cropped closer to the vessel and with slightly warmer colour: the sunburst paddlebox, the SAN RAFAEL nameboard on the deckhouse, the S.R. and SAN RAFAEL swallow-tail flags at bow and stern, the gilded eagle on the foremast, and small sailing craft in the middle distance.
visible_text: SAN RAFAEL on the hull; flags lettered S.R. and SAN RAFAEL
notes: Alternative crop of the same painting as ferries-31 — pick one.

depicts: Real photo postcard: the train ferry SOLANO photographed head-on in her slip on her final voyage, with every deck and rail packed with people waving at the camera.
details: Perhaps two hundred passengers crowd the open bow deck, the tops of the railcar roofs and the upper gallery around the pilot house. Small flags are strung along the superstructure and a large US flag hangs beneath the SOLANO nameboard. Two railcars sit on the deck behind the crowd. Timber slip walls run away on both sides; a lattice signal tower stands on the left wall. A printed caption fills the lower margin.
visible_text: TRAIN FERRY 'SOLANO' ON LAST TRIP PRIOR TO DEDICATION OF SOUTHERN PACIFIC COMPANY'S NEW $12,000,000 MARTINEZ-BENICIA BRIDGE
notes: A ferry's last run because a bridge opened — the same story the essay tells, rehearsed in 1930 at Carquinez. The crowd came to watch it end.

depicts: Book illustration: the Southern Pacific Sunset Limited standing on the apron at the Port Costa ferry terminal, about to run aboard the train ferry SOLANO. Locomotive 1131 and its cars are at the left; the ferry's pilot house looms behind at the right.
details: Tall dark timber walls of the apron frame both sides of the picture. Three or four men in overalls stand between the tracks. The tender is lettered SOUTHERN PACIFIC LINES and the locomotive carries the number 1131; a second locomotive faces the camera on the right-hand track. The pilot house nameboard reads SOLANO and the tall stacks and lattice gangway of the ferry rise behind it.
visible_text: Tender: SOUTHERN PACIFIC LINES / 1131. Ferry pilot house: SOLANO
notes: From C.J. Allen, 'The Steel Highway' (1928).

depicts: A cropped reproduction of José de Cañizares's 1781 manuscript chart of San Francisco Bay, portrait format: the whole bay drawn in ink and wash with soundings, the Golden Gate strait at the seaward end and the arms of the bay running south and north-east.
details: Spanish place names and depth figures are written across the water. Shorelines are shaded in a soft wash; the strait is drawn as a narrow neck between two headlands. Decorative cartouche and scale.
visible_text: Spanish manuscript labels and soundings throughout
notes: The geography that made ferries necessary, drawn 60 years before scheduled service began. Portrait format.

depicts: A very tall, narrow Interstate Commerce Commission valuation map of the Northwestern Pacific Railroad, running the length of the sheet: the railroad's line drawn from the bay north through Marin, Sonoma and Mendocino counties.
details: An engineering-drawing style plan with the route as a heavy line, stations, mileposts and county boundaries annotated along it. The southern terminus sits on the bay at Sausalito, where the line met the ferry to San Francisco.
visible_text: Station names, mileages and ICC valuation annotations along the route
notes: Extremely tall aspect (roughly 1:1.7 portrait even after downscaling). Best used as a detail crop or a slow vertical pan; shows why the Sausalito ferry mattered — it was the gateway to the whole redwood-country rail network.

depicts: HAER copy of a Bethlehem Shipbuilding Corporation shipyard drawing: the inboard profile of the ferry SAN MATEO, a long side elevation showing the vessel cut through longitudinally.
details: Frames, decks, engine and boiler spaces and the passenger cabins are drawn in fine line with dimensions and compartment labels. The title block sits at the lower right with the sheet number and the Union Plant, San Francisco imprint.
visible_text: Title block: BETHLEHEM SHIPBUILDING CORP, LTD. UNION PLANT, SAN FRANCISCO, CA. INBOARD PROFILE, SHEET NUMBER H-5314-11-10. Drawn by A.E. Wilson.
notes: Built at the Union Plant in San Francisco in 1922; the same vessel appears afloat in ferries-13, ferries-47 and ferries-48.

depicts: HAER copy of the Bethlehem Shipbuilding salon deck arrangement drawing for the ferry SAN MATEO: a plan view of the whole passenger deck seen from above.
details: The plan lays out the saloon seating, the deck houses, stairs, lavatories and the open guards running round the outside; each space is labelled and dimensioned. Title block lower right dated 12-6-21.
visible_text: Title block: BETHLEHEM SHIPBUILDING CORP, LTD. UNION PLANT, SAN FRANCISCO, CA. SALON DECK ARRANGEMENT, SHEET NUMBER 5314-11-84. Drawn by A.E. Wilson, dated 12-6-21.
notes: Shows how a bay ferry was actually laid out for passengers — a cutaway alternative to a photograph.

depicts: Detroit Publishing Company postcard view of the Golden Gate strait before the bridge: the water of the gate in the middle distance with the headlands closing in on either side and the open Pacific beyond.
details: Soft photochrom colouring — blue-green water, tan hills, hazy sky. Small sailing and steam craft on the water. The strait is completely empty of structure: nothing spans it.
visible_text: Printed caption on the card face
notes: The gap itself, unbridged. Postcard series number 7321, 1903-1904.

depicts: Photograph of the Southern Pacific ferry SAN MATEO under way on the bay, broadside on, with a full load of automobiles visible on her open auto deck.
details: The white two-deck superstructure runs almost the full length of the hull. Motor cars of the 1920s and 30s stand nose-to-tail on the lower deck behind the open guard rails. Smoke from the single stack. Copied for HAER with the negative border and identification number visible.
visible_text: HAER identification lettering on the negative
notes: An auto ferry doing the job the essay describes: driving your car onto a boat because there was no other way across.

depicts: The auto ferry SAN MATEO alongside a San Francisco terminal, broadside to the camera, with SOUTHERN PACIFIC GOLDEN GATE FERRIES, LTD. painted in large letters along her hull.
details: A line of 1930s automobiles stands on the open lower auto deck. The city rises behind the ferry. Photographed on 31 August 1935 by John W. Proter and copied for HAER, with the identification lettering in the negative border.
visible_text: On the hull: SOUTHERN PACIFIC GOLDEN GATE FERRIES, LTD. HAER identification lettering on the negative.
notes: The single most on-point image in the pool: the company name from the 1929 merger, painted on the boat, photographed less than two years before the bridge opened.

depicts: Oil painting by the marine artist William A. Coulter: a sailing ship passing through the Golden Gate under sail, the headlands rising on either side and open sea ahead.
details: Painterly light on the water and the cliffs; the ship heeled slightly with her canvas set. No bridge, no structure of any kind on the heads.
notes: Romantic period view of the strait as a seaway rather than a crossing. Small file (864x625).

attribution: Postcard of San Francisco Bay and Golden Gate by Pacific Novelty Company Postcards, circa 1910.
depicts: Pacific Novelty Company postcard panorama of San Francisco Bay and the Golden Gate, looking west across the water toward the strait with the city in the foreground.
details: Hand-tinted; the bay is filled with small vessels and the gate is a clear notch in the hills at the far side. The whole crossing lies open with nothing built across it.
visible_text: Printed caption on the card
notes: c.1910 postcard of the unbridged gate.

depicts: A Willard Worden pictorialist gelatin silver print, portrait format: the Ferry Building at night, the lit clock tower rising out of soft darkness with reflections on the wet plaza below.
details: Deliberately atmospheric — grain, halation around the lights, dark masses where the arcade should be. The tower is the only clearly resolved form.
notes: A rare night view of the terminal and a very different visual register from the documentary material. Portrait, and modest resolution (794x986).

attribution: California. Board of State Harbor Commissioners for San Francisco Harbor
depicts: Halftone plate from the Board of State Harbor Commissioners' 1932 biennial report showing the San Francisco waterfront with the Bay Bridge under construction, and a ferry under way in the foreground water.
details: Bridge piers and steelwork rise out of the bay behind; the ferry crosses in front of them with smoke from her stack. Piers and warehouse sheds line the shore.
notes: Official port publication, 1932 — the port authority documenting the thing that would take its ferry traffic away.

depicts: Photograph titled 'Entrance to Golden Gate and Angel Island (before the bridge)': a broad view across the water toward the strait, with Angel Island in the middle distance and the gate opening between the headlands beyond.
details: Bare, treeless brown hills on both sides of the strait. Sailing craft and a small steamer on the water. The headlands where the bridge towers would later stand are completely undeveloped. Soft, slightly hazy contrast typical of a turn-of-the-century print.
notes: C.C. Pierce. The literal 'before' shot the theme needs. A second, near-identical exposure of this scene existed on Commons; the better print was kept.

depicts: C.R. Savage photograph of the Golden Gate seen from the Cliff House side: a rocky promontory in the foreground with the water of the strait beyond and a vessel on it.
details: Dramatic dark rock mass at the left; the far headland is a low silhouette across the water. No bridge, no structure. The original catalogue note points out explicitly that no bridge is visible.
visible_text: Front label on the mount: C.R. Savage, Photo, Salt Lake.
notes: c.1894 — the strait as it looked a generation before anyone proposed spanning it.

depicts: Halftone from Railway and Locomotive Engineering (1902) showing a narrow-gauge steam locomotive and train of the line that connected with the Sausalito ferry, photographed side-on.
details: A small tank-and-tender engine with a diamond stack and its wooden coaches, crew posed alongside. Trackside timber structures behind.
visible_text: Journal caption below the plate
notes: The Marin railroad half of the journey: passengers came off the ferry at Sausalito and onto a train like this.

depicts: Plate from the 1914 Chamber of Commerce Handbook for San Francisco, portrait format: a Mount Tamalpais gravity car loaded with day-trippers on the Mill Valley and Mt Tamalpais Scenic Railway, high on the mountain with the bay visible below.
details: Passengers in hats and coats sit in open tiered rows on the car; a gripman stands at the brake at the front. The track curves round a bare hillside; the bay and its far shore lie hazy in the distance.
visible_text: Book caption below the plate
notes: The Marin excursion trade the ferries fed — the tourism argument the bridge campaign later borrowed. Portrait format.

attribution: Charles S. Bulkley (C.E.); L.H. Shortt & S.R. Throckmorton Jr., engineers; H. Alricks Jr., topographer; lith. G.T. Brown & Co., San Francisco. David Rumsey Map Collection, Stanford Libraries.
depicts: Lithographed survey map, 'Map of Lands of the Saucelito Land and Ferry Company', showing the company's holdings on the Marin shore laid out in numbered lots and blocks around Richardson's Bay, with the shoreline, wharf and street grid drawn in.
details: Fine engraved linework with lot numbers, acreages, a title cartouche naming the engineers and the lithographer, and a north arrow. The plan runs from the waterfront up over the hills; the ferry landing point is shown on the bay.
visible_text: Map of Lands of the Saucelito Land and Ferry Company As Laid Out Under The Direction of Chas. S. Bulkley C.E.; L.H. Shortt ... Lith. G.T. Brown & Co., San Francisco.
notes: The company named in the research, on its own 1868 promotional survey — the land speculation that the ferry existed to serve. Licence is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (David Rumsey Map Collection), not public domain: credit is required.

depicts: Colour transparency of the San Francisco Embarcadero from Pioneer Park on Telegraph Hill, looking south-east: the row of numbered finger piers runs down the left, the Ferry Building sits in the middle distance and the Bay Bridge crosses the background.
details: Piers 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 15 and 17 are visible in sequence along the waterfront with ships alongside. The Ferry Building's tower is now a small element in a working cargo port rather than the focus of the shot. Downtown blocks rise on the right.
notes: 1953, from a private slide collection digitised on the Internet Archive; rights are uploader-asserted rather than a formal licence, so treat as unclear. Downscaled from a 13,000 px scan.

attribution: Carleton Watkins (American, 1829 - 1916) (1829 - 1916) – photographer (American) Details on Google Art Project
depicts: Carleton Watkins mammoth-plate albumen photograph looking north across the water from San Francisco to Sausalito, Richardson's Bay and Mount Tamalpais rising behind.
details: A wide, quiet composition: flat water across the whole lower half, the Marin shore as a low dark band, and the bare pyramid of Tamalpais on the skyline. Sausalito is a scatter of small buildings along the waterline — almost nothing there. Watkins's characteristic long tonal range and enormous detail.
notes: The Marin shore as it looked when the ferry company was young: the destination the boats served, still barely settled.

depicts: A newspaper advertisement clipped from The Daily Examiner, tall narrow portrait format: the North Pacific Coast Railroad's timetable and fare table for March 1887, set in dense period display type.
details: Column of departure times headed by the ferry connection from San Francisco, with the boat and train schedule for Saucelito, San Rafael, Tomales, Point Reyes and the northern stations, plus round-trip fares. Rules and bold headings break the column into sections.
visible_text: North Pacific Coast Railroad schedule and rates for March 1887 — departure times, station list and fares
notes: The closest thing in the pool to a period timetable: the actual advertised boat-and-train schedule out of San Francisco to Marin, 1887. Very tall portrait.
